key_insight: Eliminating plateauing operators during ADAPT-VQE and combining the ansatz with correlated downfolding can make quantum chemistry optimization faster, shallower, and more accurate within a fixed active space.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a practical path to lower circuit depth and fewer iterations for near-term quantum hardware while improving energy estimates without expanding the active-space size.
method: Detect and remove non-contributing operators from the ADAPT-VQE pool when parameters stall.
Compare operator elimination with and without pool restoration during optimization.
Integrate ADAPT-VQE with one-body downfolding (OBDF) to fold environmental dynamical correlation into an effective active-space Hamiltonian.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on linear H6, H6 lattice, H6 ring, and N2 using OpenFermion show reduced depth and iteration count, and OBDF-ADAPT-VQE gives energies closer to FCI than standard ADAPT-VQE in the same active space.
watch_item: Operator elimination and OBDF depend on reliable detection of plateaus and effective Hamiltonian construction, so performance may vary with system choice and active-space quality.
paper_title: Reducing quantum resources for ADAPT-VQE via plateau-operator elimination and correlated mean-field downfolding
